### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e5cf27d65fc28cf0a351cb2b6a616998d81ff0d8`.

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e5cf27d65fc28cf0a351cb2b6a616998d81ff0d8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8f93f8b35413d9bb015c2228dbf7d26ad16fd359` — the merge of head `6368aa57a44c349de8104cd84d83773143cbd9c3` into base `e5cf27d65fc28cf0a351cb2b6a616998d81ff0d8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8f93f8b35413d9bb015c2228dbf7d26ad16fd359 && git checkout 8f93f8b35413d9bb015c2228dbf7d26ad16fd359
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e5cf27d65fc28cf0a351cb2b6a616998d81ff0d8 6368aa57a44c349de8104cd84d83773143cbd9c3 && git checkout -B drift-repro e5cf27d65fc28cf0a351cb2b6a616998d81ff0d8 && git merge --no-ff 6368aa57a44c349de8104cd84d83773143cbd9c3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e5cf27d65fc28cf0a351cb2b6a616998d81ff0d8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e5cf27d65fc28cf0a351cb2b6a616998d81ff0d8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 78/78 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f35d38b16dc4acb52a5e4f88c5771114069102a6`

### ① Derived judgments

0. **BLOCKING (② carrier).** `.changeset/20150-import-mapping-target-names-a-field.md:15` reads bare `Clause-②: yes`; the PR body reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. AGENTS.md §Post-Task 3 (l.1085-1086): the changeset body "also carries the PR's `Clause-②` line: `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` reads the arm there". That gate (`breakingDeclaration` → `readClause2Line(parsed.body)`, changeset carrier) sees no arm; it classified the changeset breaking only through signal (2), the free-form `**BREAKING**` banner, the carrier #16421 named weakest. Fix: change line 15 to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. Nothing else changes.
1. **One predicate.** `unknownImportMappingTargets` is the only verdict: rest `refuseUnknownMappingTargets` (import-mapping.ts) and lint `validateMappingTargetFields` both call it; lint's dotted-head branch only shapes the message. `packages/cli/src` reads no `fieldMapping` (grep 0); spec has no other reader (conversions hits are fixtures/connector `fieldMappings`).
2. **Admitted set = engine.** `undeclaredWriteFieldErrors` (engine.ts:1579-1610) admits keys of `_registry.getObject(object).fields` (post `applySystemFields`, which consumes `resolveInjectedSystemColumns`, registry.ts:508) ∪ `id/created_at/updated_at`, and has no opinion on an absent/empty map. The predicate is declared ∪ plan.names ∪ the same three, null on absent/empty. At the door the body is `getMetaItem().item`, folded via `registry.foldObjectExtendersOnto` (protocol.ts:7056-7058), so `objectExtensions` fields are present; `owner_id` follows the plan exactly (absent under `ownership:'none'`, `managedBy`, `sys_*`). The `task` fixture is `systemFields:false` (import-integration.test.ts:63), so the `created_at` control is real. No false refusal found. Residual (door admits, engine refuses): a map-form def whose `name` differs from its key is admitted under both spellings (import-mapping-target.ts:1148) while the engine reads keys only.
3. **Door.** Refusal sits after the 413 row cap and before `applyMappingToRows`, inside the one function both `POST :object/import` (rest-server.ts:9762) and `/import/jobs` (:9865) call: dryRun, commit and async byte-identical, no job row created. The schema fetch was already unconditional, so hoisting adds no work; a refused mapping skips the per-row apply. One observable change: a mapping with both an unsupported transform and a bad target now answers `INVALID_FIELD` instead of `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM`. Every string element of a `split` array is judged; non-strings are left to the schema. When `getMetaItem` throws, `schema` stays undefined and the door is silent, i.e. behaves as before; silence matches the engine and is right.
4. **Author-time.** `path` is `mappings[i].fieldMapping[j].target[k]`, severity `error`. Skip 1 matches `validateObjectFieldRefs`/`validateListViewFieldRefs`, which read `asArray(stack.objects)` only. Held to one gate set by the `REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_RULES` entry in `AUTHORING_RULES` (`commands: ALL`); `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` governs only hand-wired non-registry gates, so it is the registry ratchet, not that file, that holds it. `recordsOf` keeps map keys as `name`, so the extension fold is sound; no shared lint fold helper exists, so it is not a second copy.
5. **#20149 seam.** One marked arm in `judgeImportMappingTarget` (l.1176-1181), `index.fields` carries declared defs. But the lint message sentence "a dotted path into a field's value is not a target" restates the no-parts rule in prose and must be rewritten when #20149 lands.
6. **Truth.** Changeset and docblocks check out (barrel `data/index.ts:171` re-exports `mapping.zod`, which re-exports the module). Summary line `fix(rest,lint)` omits spec, which also gains exports; cosmetic.

### ② Semver level

`minor` ×3 right: spec widens public surface (yes ⇒ ≥ minor), rest/lint narrow an accept set (BREAKING banner, launch window). ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` right: body carries no FROM→TO, arrow rewrite or migration table; nothing authorable renamed; refused mappings already failed every row. `yes (narrowing)` is the grammar's own row for widen-and-narrow (clause2-line.mjs). Carriers: `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads the PR body from the event payload (`yes` ⇒ ≥ minor, satisfied); `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads the changeset body (arm absent, see item 0). Both green in `Lint & Repo Gates`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Docs `import-mappings.mdx` §Rejections (l.210-224) and `defineStack()` list (l.55-60): incomplete, no sentence false; the per-row "engine rejected the record" row stays true. Docs PR after #20170.
- `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS` is a non-exported const (engine.ts:1579); the spec mirror is pinned only by spec's own test, drift possible both ways. Later card: engine imports the spec constant.
- Runtime publish gate note correct: member keeps `['flow']`; a runtime-saved bad mapping is refused at use.
- `upsertKey` → `matchFields` → `findExisting` where-filter (import-runner.ts:484-490) unjudged; dry-run parity there unpinned. Separate card.
- Inline `mapping` renames and raw headers naming no field still pass dryRun and fail on commit; outside this card, #4633 gap persists there.
- Lint-only false finding possible when an object has extensions and a field def's `name` differs from its key (`recordsOf` spread drops the key); rare.
- Array-form `fields`: engine silent, predicate judges; unreachable at the door (registry bodies are records).
- CI at review: 41/44 green or skipped; `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace` still running.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 87/87 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6368aa57a44c349de8104cd84d83773143cbd9c3`

### ① Derived judgments
1. Previous blocking item RESOLVED. `git diff f35d38b1..6368aa57` touches only `.changeset/20150-import-mapping-target-names-a-field.md` (2 lines): `Clause-②: yes` → `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, summary scope `fix(rest,lint)` → `fix(spec,rest,lint)`. PR body carries the identical `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. `check-adr-0087-registration` run read-only on a detached head with `--base e4471e64` (merge base): exit 0, classification line `.changeset/20150-import-mapping-target-names-a-field.md  [BREAKING+clause-②-narrowing]  not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Grammar per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: `yes (narrowing)` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; this diff adds 8 public `@objectstack/spec` exports (api-surface +8) and narrows the import door and lint accept set, so it is the right arm.
2. Summary line true: the diff moves src in all three packages, the refusal sits in `prepareImportRequest` which both `rest-server.ts` call sites use (`:9762` sync dry run and commit, `:9865` async jobs), and the lint member joins the suite `os validate` shares. Every other changeset sentence verified against source, with one overstatement carried to ③ (the "never refuses a target the import door accepts" sentence).
3. One predicate: `unknownImportMappingTargets` in `packages/spec/src/data/import-mapping-target.ts`, reached via `mapping.zod.ts` `export *` and the data barrel (pinned). rest calls it once (`refuseUnknownMappingTargets`); lint calls it plus `indexImportMappingTargets` for the hint only. `import-runner.ts` / `previewVerdict` untouched; no second parser anywhere.
4. Admitted set vs engine door: `engine.ts:1579-1591` `undeclaredWriteFieldErrors` admits map keys ∪ `id, created_at, updated_at`, no opinion on an empty or non-map field set. Spec index = map keys ∪ `name` aliases ∪ `resolveInjectedSystemColumns().names` ∪ the same three; null on empty/unreadable. Never narrower than the door (safe direction only).
5. Door refusal identical: one function, both routes map `!prep.ok` to `res.status(prep.status).json({code, error})`; integration test pins `dry._json` equal to `commit._json`, nothing written. The `metaMap` block never reads `rows`, so moving `applyMappingToRows` below it is behavior-preserving; only ordering changes (bad target now refused before an unsupported transform).
6. Author-time rule and gate set: member of `REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_RULES`, no `runtimeTypes` so `DEFAULT_MEMBER_RUNTIME_TYPES = ['flow']` applies as the changeset states. `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` enumerates no rule names; no catalog outside lint lists rule ids (`dataset-field-unknown` appears only in lint CHANGELOG and one protocol test). Finding shape matches `DatasetRefFinding`. `recordsOf` names map-form fields, so the extension fold is sound.
7. #20149 seam: single marked arm in `judgeImportMappingTarget`; `ImportMappingTargetIndex.fields` carries declared definitions only (pinned); dotted target pinned `unknown`.
8. Docblock truth: module claims verified against `engine.ts`, `injected-system-columns.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `SystemFieldName` (`id`/`created_at`/`updated_at`). Merge onto `origin/main` is clean (`merge-tree`: 0 conflicts; main's baseline additions are unrelated entries).

### ② Semver level
`minor` ×3 is correct: AGENTS.md §3 says `yes` takes at least `minor` and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, shipped `minor` in the launch window. Carriers: `check-changeset-no-major` reads the PR BODY (`declarationFromPullRequest` → `readClause2Line(pr.body)`); local run exit 0: "declares clause-② `yes (narrowing)`, and no package whose src it moves is graded `patch`". `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the CHANGESET body: `breakingDeclaration` signals `BREAKING` (banner) and `clause-②-narrowing` (arm) → disposition required → `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` accepted (no FROM→TO prescription in the body). Both gates' self-tests pin `yes (narrowing)` as MUST_MATCH. CI at head: `Check Changeset` success; 25 success / 3 skipped / 6 in progress (Test Core ×5, Lint & Repo Gates), 0 failed.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Previous record not present on the PR (0 reviews, 0 review comments); every item above re-judged from scratch, none carried.
- Changeset sentence "it never refuses a target the import door accepts" holds for metadata-declared fields (authored plus folded `objectExtensions`), not for fields a plugin injects imperatively at runtime, which the rule's own docblock names; smallest fix: append "among the fields the stack's metadata declares". Non-blocking: sibling field-existence rules share the limit.
- PR title says `fix(rest,lint)` while the changeset says `fix(spec,rest,lint)`; no gate reads the title.
- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`: the "Rejections before any row is read" table lacks the new 400 `INVALID_FIELD` row and the build-validation list lacks the rule; no sentence turns false; frontmatter held by #20170; docs follow-on.
- When `getMetaItem` / `getObjectSchema` fail, `schema` is undefined and the door has no opinion, so the old dry-run/commit divergence persists there (the engine's own position).
- Spec verdict can be wider than the door (a `name` alias, or an injected-plan column absent from the registered map); never narrower.
- Engine keeps its own `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS` literal; the spec constant mirrors it, no shared source.
- `mapping` runtime writes are not judged at the publish gate (flow default); the door refuses at use. `upsertKey` naming no field is not judged.
- Refusal order: a bad target now answers `INVALID_FIELD` before `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` on the same mapping.
